item.title: Saturday, September 12, 2026 - Bike Filming from Alaska to Tierra Del Fuego, Delhi to Sweden 26/36
item.description: Bike Talk! celebrates bike rides, collectives, activists, artists, commuters, enthusiasts, professional cyclists, inventors, mechanics, and the bicycle itself as a human-powered mode of transportation.
item.itunes:summary:
2:30 Jonathan Hale of People’s Vision Zero at a “ghost tire” placing on Forest Lawn Drive in Los Angeles, to honor 70-year-old Bijan Yousefian, a victim of traffic violence who died in a fiery crash there.

  6:25 High School senior Ben Mangiafico talks about the bike ride he hosted recently to point out the dangerous spots on his route to school.

12:45 Dr. Timm Döbert and Leanna Carriere on their 9-month, 30,000km ride from Alaska’s High Arctic to Tierra del Fuego to follow the migration of Hudsonian Whimbrels, and Wings of Survival, the documentary about their journey.  

25:30 Bicycle Film Festival Director Brendt Barbur on the Festival’s 26 year history and this year’s offerings. 

40:06 Another bike film, The Cycle of Love (2025), is a documentary about a man who rode 6,000 miles from Delhi to Sweden in 1977 in search of a woman he believed was prophesied to be his wife. Director Orlando von Einsiedel talks with us about his film.

53:55 News: 
Berkeley sued over Hopkins bike lane plan
MIT professor dies of injuries after being struck by a driver while cycling on Memorial Drive
Folsom considers crackdown on e-bike wheelies, stunts and unsafe riding
Japan halves speed limit to 30km/h on all narrow city streets

item.title: Saturday, September 5, 2026 - Streetfilms NYC, Anti-bike lane bill in LA 26/35
item.description: Bike Talk! celebrates bike rides, collectives, activists, artists, commuters, enthusiasts, professional cyclists, inventors, mechanics, and the bicycle itself as a human-powered mode of transportation.
item.itunes:summary:
2:45 Language was added to a bill targeting a much needed protected bike lane and traffic calming project on LA’s high speed Forest Lawn Drive, where there have been more than 95 crashes and 4 fatalities since 2013. The bill was paid for by Forest Lawn Cemetery donations, and it’ll be an issue in the LA Mayoral race, says Michael Schneider of Streets For All. 

12:19 LA Metro will pay some drivers to drive less in a new program, as the city looks toward a more car-light 2028 Olympics. LA Metro spokesperson Patrick Chandler gives the details. 

21:55 Streetfilms filmmaker Clarence Eckerson talks with Taylor about his work as an urbanist educator.

45:55 News: 
Pedestrian pronounced dead after Tour de Fat vehicle crash, 5 remain injured, in unknown condition
New Illinois law sets license, insurance requirements for e-bike riders
Newport Beach residents frustrated by e-bikes parked in front of their homes
Bill to strengthen walking and biking programs, AB 2168, headed to governor’s desk
Cyclists have crashed on Market Street’s rail tracks for 130 years. Why can’t SF fix them?

49:08 More eulogies from Bike Oven/ Killradio/ Bike Talk/ bike community documentarian and spirit-booster DJ Chickenleather’s memorial at the Highland Park Bike Oven.

item.title: Saturday, August 29, 2026 - The Journey Makes The Hero 26/34
item.description: Bike Talk! celebrates bike rides, collectives, activists, artists, commuters, enthusiasts, professional cyclists, inventors, mechanics, and the bicycle itself as a human-powered mode of transportation.
item.itunes:summary:
2:10 Chickenleather, spirit and documentarian of the LA bike movement for decades, died last week. We bring you his words from 2010 on getting “normal” people to bike, engaging the youth, and volunteering at a bike collective. 

  7:12 Taylor drafts behind yet another stranger, Josep in Cataluña, Spain, and they talk afterward. 

12:25 Bike Talk listener Tim Dyet says he’s inspired by Taylor Nichols’ ride from SF to Michigan to do a 10 day ride of his own along the Empire Trail bike path in New York.

17:45 Team Samaritan riders Tom Schwein and David McKean aim to raise two million dollars with a Ride Across America for Catholic Charities to help fight the nation’s homeless epidemic.

33:00 Massachusetts Streetsblog reporter and editor Christian MilNeil on the elimination of a Boston bikeway by the Mayor Wu administration.

46:01 News: 
3 Cyclists Die in One Week in Hit-and-Runs in New York City.
Against Neighbors’ Wishes, Boston Streets Commissioners Cancel Planned Bikeway Near Day Square.
E-bikes, scooters, boards prohibited at all of Newport-Mesa Unified’s K-8 campuses. 
Como mayor bans bikes in city centre after being hit ‘by one of these beasts’.
LA Mayor hits brakes on needed bike lanes near Forest Lawn. Mayoral opponent Raman is slamming her for it.

48:39 Chickenleather’s memorial at the Bike Oven in Highland Park, Los Angeles.

item.title: Saturday, August 22, 2026 - Backpedaling 26/33
item.description: Bike Talk! celebrates bike rides, collectives, activists, artists, commuters, enthusiasts, professional cyclists, inventors, mechanics, and the bicycle itself as a human-powered mode of transportation.
item.itunes:summary:
Taylor rides Barcelona, and says it’s civilized.

  4:15 A Quebec court rules against Toronto’s famously successful protected lanes. Michael Longfield, Executive Director of Cycle Toronto, explains. 

15:28 NYC closes a 1 block gap in Ashland Avenue’s protected bike lane in Brooklyn, known as “Crashland” for the danger created when Mayor Adams’ corrupt administration blocked that part of the path. Streetsblog NYC reporters Emily Lipstein and Michael Duggan fill in the gaps. 

20:25 A fully funded safety improvement project on Forest Lawn Drive was stopped by LA Mayor Bass despite years of public planning, extensive community outreach, and documented safety concerns. Streets Are For Everyone ED Damian Kevitt breaks it down.

26:37 News:
Driver Hits 11, Kills Two College Cyclists in Tennessee'''.
The car killing of British rider Fin Tarling during Friday’s stage of the Volta a Portugal.
'''Bike-hating Ontario Premier Doug Ford wins court battle to strip Toronto of its main downtown bike lanes.
London’s Cycleway network grows five-fold in decade to 450km'''.

28:44 Riders of the “friendly 8” in Halcyon, New Jersey, Kimberly Organo-Solo and Charles Sontag, with ride leader Lo Sontag, on why they ride and don’t ride more. 

39:19 Owner of Allez LA bike shop in Los Angeles, Kyle Kelley, whom interviewer Jim Cadenhead calls “the most famous fixie foo that ever was”.

42:40 Erasure poetry from bike hate mail submissions by Liza Birch, a Rhode Island bike advocate.

item.title: Saturday, August 15, 2026 - Beyond Cyclists 26/32
item.description: Bike Talk! celebrates bike rides, collectives, activists, artists, commuters, enthusiasts, professional cyclists, inventors, mechanics, and the bicycle itself as a human-powered mode of transportation.
item.itunes:summary:
2:15 Walk Bike Berkeley organizer Ben Gerhardstein on why Berkeley needs the Hopkins Ave protected bike lane they fought for so long to get and finally won, and why the opposition was so vitriolic. 

  6:30 A recent study, “Beyond Cyclists,” finds that support for and opposition to cycling infrastructure don’t always follow intuitive lines, and the ways pro-bike arguments are framed matters. Quebecois researchers Jérôme Laviolette, Kevin Manaugh, Owen Waygood unpack their study.

35:05 Our bike lawyer Jim Pocrass talks with our news anchor, Stacey Randecker, about her e-bike crash, her medical treatment, her settlement, and why every document mattered. 

44:30 News: 
Amazon responds to Mamdani’s cease-and-desist letter.
A Boston City Official Wants Cars To Stop Blocking Bike Lanes And Crosswalks.
Durham Dedicates $1M To Protecting Bike Lanes.
UT Austin officials say a new mobility plan is coming as cyclists worry about potential bike ban.

47:35 Fresno County’s Board of Supervisors buried Measure C, a transportation tax favoring local roads and transit over freeway expansion, using a procedural trick. A law just signed by California Governor Newsom would foil the Board and put Measure C on Fresno’s ballot in November. The Supes plan to sue, claiming the law is unconstitutional. Fresnoland’s Editor in Chief Danielle Bergstrom reports.

item.title: Saturday, August 8, 2026 - We’re Not Copenhagen 26/31
item.description: Bike Talk! celebrates bike rides, collectives, activists, artists, commuters, enthusiasts, professional cyclists, inventors, mechanics, and the bicycle itself as a human-powered mode of transportation.
item.itunes:summary:
Taylor on being a bike nerd and making friends by bike, like Kay Shuster. 

  5:41 Bicycles Are Partisan now, writes Lo Sontag in light of the MAGA federal assault on biking. But the real divide isn’t left/right, it’s who has power and who doesn’t. 

19:45 Listener Tim Dyet writes he plans a bike trip in NY, inspired by Taylor’s recent ride from SF to Michigan. Tim plans to take his bike on an Amtrak train – speaking of which, the League of American Bicyclists has issued a report on bike-friendly trains. 

24:27 Nietifa, a listener, suggests a “limited license” for bad drivers.

25:55 In “The Social Cost of Automobility, Cycling and Walking in the European Union,” Swedish researcher Stephan Gosling says that in advocating for bike infrastructure, we shouldn’t argue against cars.

41:26 Stacey’s News: After years of debate, Berkeley approves Hopkins bike lanes.
Archer Ave Bike Lanes Tension Fuels Political Ambitions in Chicago.
A woman in a Queens bike lane was fatally struck by an SUV driver who never stopped.
Pedestrians and cyclists can cross the Gordie Howe International Bridge for free in Detroit.

44:27 Berkeley’s long overdue approval of the Hopkins Avenue protected bike lane – with Robert Prinz, Bike East Bay.

item.title: Saturday, August 1, 2026 - Bike Hope Versus Bike Hate 26/30
item.description: Bike Talk! celebrates bike rides, collectives, activists, artists, commuters, enthusiasts, professional cyclists, inventors, mechanics, and the bicycle itself as a human-powered mode of transportation.
item.itunes:summary:
6:50 The USDOT/FHWA removed  bike lanes, road diets, and speed management tools that have been shown to reduce traffic injuries and fatalities from their list of Proven Safety Countermeasures on USDOT/FHWA sites. Is the administration anti-safety? Of course, as League of American Bicyclists Deputy Executive Director Caron Whitaker explains, the Proven Safety Countermeasures’ removal by USDOT does not change the fact that they make roads safer. 

17:54 Bike share is transportation! Recognizing this, bike-sharing Brooklyn Councilmember Lincoln Restler has a bill to cap Citibike fares at the price of a bus or subway. Lincoln talks about CD 33’s other bike/active transportation/safe streets initiatives, too.

36:08 San Francisco architect Ben Frommagen is on a 4,200 + day streak of riding every day for two hours (almost 12 years). Taylor rides along with Ben and talks over coffee about the personal, mental and physical trade-offs of keeping the streak.
